children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:

** South Korean shares rose on Monday, driven by chipmakers on optimism around strong demand for AI investments, while the won hit a near two-year high amid expectations of continued dollar selling by major exporters.
** The benchmark KOSPI
was up 196.57 points, or 2.94%, at 6,883.78, as of 0123 GMT. Earlier in the session, it rose as much as 3.5% to hit its highest intraday level since August 27.
** Wall Street weakened on Friday, but the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index
was a clear outperformer, gaining 3.4%.
** South Korea's exports so far this year have surpassed last year's annual record, as the economy rides high on booming global demand for AI chips.
** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics
rose 3.72% and peer SK Hynix
gained 6.01%, leading the benchmark index higher.
** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution
climbed 0.14%, while Hyundai Motor
and sister automaker Kia Corp
were up 1.69% and 0.32%, respectively.
** Steelmaker POSCO Holdings
shed 1.19%, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics
rose 0.14%.
** Of the total 909 traded issues, 438 shares advanced, while 406 declined.
** Foreigners were net buyers of shares worth 789.2 billion won ($590.45 million).
** The won was quoted at 1,335.8 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, 1.07% higher than its previous close at 1,350.1. The won hit its strongest level since October 2024.
** In money and debt markets, September futures on three-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) gained 0.07 point to 103.24.
** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) fell by 0.8 basis point to 3.875%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
fell by 2.7 basis points to 4.334%.
